findings.reason: a node following the split literally reaches the block with no way to count first-attempt passes and must either deviate or move the count into _candidates_scan, so the section must settle where passed_first_attempt is counted (and whether the scan also collects a passed-row subset) before it is dispatched.
findings.text: the deliverable assigns _candidates_scan to collect "each matched row's attempt" (necessarily a flat, row-agnostic list, because the same bullet's sibling test expects attempts_median 3 from the values 1, 3 and 7 together — the failed row's attempt included) but assigns passed_first_attempt — "the matched rows whose gate is passed and whose attempt is 1" — to _requirement_block, which receives only that row-agnostic list plus the gate Counter and so cannot join a gate to an attempt; with a flat list the block can compute attempts_median but never the gate-conditioned count
